et_pb_bg_layout_light"><div class="et_pb_text_inner"><h2><span style="font-size: xx-large;">On this page</span></h2><ul><li><span style="font-size: large;"><a href="#Governing"><span style="font-weight: 400; font-family: Arial;"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Part 1: Governing principles and guidelines</span></span></a></span></li><li><span style="font-size: large;"><a href="#Part2"><span style="font-weight: 400; font-family: Arial;"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Part 2 and on</span></span></a></span></li><li><span style="font-size: large;"><a href="#Implementing"><span style="font-weight: 400; font-family: Arial;"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Implementing the standard</span></span></a></span></li><li><span style="font-size: large;"><a href="#Implementing"><span style="font-weight: 400; font-family: Arial;"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Repository of supporting documents</span></span></a></span></li><li><span style="font-size: large;"><a href="#History"><span style="font-weight: 400; font-family: Arial;"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">History of the standard</span></span></a></span></li></ul><p><span style="font-weight: 400;"></span></p><p>The International Plain Language Federation initiated a project to create a plain language standard through the International Organization for Standardization (ISO). Plain language experts decided to do the standard through ISO for two reasons:</p><ul><li>the credibility of ISO, which has a network of over 174 national standards bodies and more than 26,000 standards</li><li>the credibility of being developed with input and support from many plain language experts around the world</li></ul><p>A plain language standard provides a clear understanding of what plain language is and how you can achieve it.</p><p>Before the standard was published, there were no universally agreed-on principles for creating plain language documents or for determining whether something is plain. This made it difficult for people writing and designing documents to assess the quality of their processes and their documents. Having an international standard means that everyone can now work from the same understanding.</p><p><span></span></p></div></div></div></div><div class="et_pb_row et_pb_row_2"><div class="et_pb_column et_pb_column_4_4 et_pb_column_2  et_pb_css_mix_blend_mode_passthrough et-last-child"><div id="Governing" class="et_pb_module et_pb_text et_pb_text_2  et_pb_text_align_left et_pb_bg_layout_light"><div class="et_pb_text_inner"><h2><span><span style="font-size: xx-large;"><strong></strong></span></span></h2><h2><span style="font-size: xx-large;">Part 1: Governing principles and guidelines</span></h2><p>In 2023, ISO published the plain language standard called <a href="https://bit.ly/42PqTdA"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">ISO 24495-1:2023 Plain language — Part 1: Governing principles and guidelines</span></a>.</p><p>These 4 four principles in the standard give details on what methods you can use to write a plain language document:</p><ul><li>Readers get what they need (relevant)</li><li>Readers can easily find what they need (findable)</li><li>Readers can easily understand what they find (understandable)</li><li>Readers can easily use the information (usable)</li></ul><p><span></span></p></div></div><div class="et_pb_button_module_wrapper et_pb_button_0_wrapper  et_pb_module "> <a class="et_pb_button et_pb_button_0 et_animated et_hover_enabled et_pb_bg_layout_light" href="https://www.iplfederation.org/press-release-part1/" data-icon="$" data-animation-style="fade" data-animation-repeat="" data-animation-duration="1000ms" data-animation-delay="0ms" data-animation-intensity="50%" data-animation-starting-opacity="0%" data-animation-speed-curve="ease-in-out">Read the press release</a></div><div class="et_pb_module et_pb_text et_pb_text_3  et_pb_text_align_left et_pb_bg_layout_light"><div class="et_pb_text_inner"><h3><span style="font-size: x-large;"><strong>Based on research and consensus</strong></span></h3><p>Part 1 of the standard is based on empirical evidence and on the <a href="https://www.iplfederation.org/plain-language-definitions/"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">definition of plain language</span></a> that experts adopted in 2014. In addition, it was created using ISO’s well-regarded consensus model. Experts from 25 countries (representing 19 languages) drafted and approved the standard. Because of all of this work that was done together, plain language practitioners around the world support this standard.</p><p>The other parts to the standard were written using the same model.</p><p>We’ve published a <a href="https://www.iplfederation.org/bibliography-iso/"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">bibliography</span> </a>of some of the research that the standard is based on.</p><h3><span style="font-size: x-large;"><strong></strong></span></h3><h3><span style="font-size: x-large;"><strong>Works in most languages</strong></span></h3><p>The standard is not just for English, nor is it just for ISO’s other two official languages, French and Russian. In fact, the standard is language neutral. So it works in most languages and across all sectors.</p><p>50 plain language experts from 25 countries drafted and approved the standard (representing 19 languages). Through the commenting practice used in the ISO consensus model, they were able to make sure every part of the standard works in their languages.</p><p>Some countries will localize the standard, to add information that’s specific to a language or to a country. Countries may also develop best practices to reflect what works within their own language, such as sentence length.</p><h3><span style="font-size: x-large;"><strong></strong></span></h3><h3><span style="font-size: x-large;"><strong>More than just words </strong></span></h3><p><span style="font-weight: 400;">The guidance in the standard includes many plain language practices that are not word related. The ISO standard has roughly 485 ideas. These cover a variety of language issues (such as the content’s structure, findability, understandability, and usability) but <a href="https://www.iplfederation.org/word-choice"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">only 7% focus on word choice</span></a>. We came to this conclusion by analyzing the words and ideas in the standard.</span></p><p><span style="font-weight: 400;">And the guidance that does relate to words is high level, so it’s not specific to any one language. For example, the standard talks about using culturally relevant language, using words that your readers know, and using clear sentences.</span></p><p><span style="font-weight: 400;"></span></p><p><span></span></p></div></div><div id="Part2" class="et_pb_module et_pb_text et_pb_text_4  et_pb_text_align_left et_pb_bg_layout_light"><div class="et_pb_text_inner"><h2><span style="font-size: xx-large;"></span></h2><h2><span style="font-size: xx-large;">Part 2: Legal communication</span></h2><p>ISO published <a href="bit.ly/3HTq12X"><span style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">ISO 24495-2:2025 Plain language — Part 2: Legal communication</span></span></a> in August 2025.</p><p>Part 2 deals with legal communication, and it builds on the foundation for plain language in ISO 24495-1. It establishes guidelines and techniques to help authors make sure that readers can readily understand legal communication and exercise their legal rights and obligations.</p><p>It explains how to apply principles from ISO 24495-1 in legal contexts that require authors to achieve these goals:</p><ul><li>reach multiple audiences with different needs</li><li>adhere to legally required structural and design requirements</li><li>explain complex and nuanced legal concepts</li><li>explain processes that readers must navigate to exercise legal rights and obligations.     </li></ul><p>The document applies to legal documents in all sectors, including the legal, governmental, non-governmental and health sectors.<span style="text-decoration: line-through;"></span></p><p>Read the press release in <a href="https://www.iplfederation.org/press-release-part-2/"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">English</span></a>, <span style="text-decoration: underline;"><a href="https://www.iplfederation.org/press-release-part-2-french/">French</a></span>, <span style="text-decoration: underline;"><a href="https://www.iplfederation.org/press-release-part-2-italian/">Italian</a></span> and <span style="text-decoration: underline;"><a href="https://www.iplfederation.org/press-release-part-2-spanish/">Spanish</a></span>.</p><p> </p><h2><span style="font-size: xx-large;">Part 3: Science writing</span></h2><p>ISO published <span style="text-decoration: underline;"><a href="https://bit.ly/42uJEVO">ISO 24495-3:2026 Plain language — Part 3: Science writing</a></span> in May 2026. </p><p>Part 3 deals with science writing, and it builds on the foundation for plain language in ISO 24495-1.</p><p>It focuses on <strong>science</strong> writing: writing about scientific subjects that is intended for readers with varying education levels, backgrounds and interests. These readers can range from young students to decision-makers in industry and government.</p><ul><li>This part does not explicitly address <strong>scientific</strong> writing. Such writing is found in scientific journal articles or academic documents, where experts write for others in their fields of specialization.</li><li>However, it is possible that other experts do not work in precisely the same field as the author and prefer reading documents that follow plain language guidance.</li></ul><p><span>This document applies to printed or digital information that is primarily in the form of text and images.</span></p><p>Read the press release in <span style="text-decoration: underline;"><a href="https://www.iplfederation.org/press-release-part-3/">English</a></span>, <span style="text-decoration: underline;"><a href="https://www.iplfederation.org/press-release-part-3-french/">French</a></span>, <span style="text-decoration: underline;"><a href="https://www.iplfederation.org/press-release-part-3-italian/">Italian</a></span> and <span style="text-decoration: underline;"><a href="https://www.iplfederation.org/press-release-part-3-spanish/">Spanish</a></span>. </p><p> </p><h2 style="background: #ffffff; font-family: Arial, serif;"><span style="font-size: xx-large;">Notation for business reporting</span></h2><p><span style="font-weight: 400;">ISO published <span style="text-decoration: underline;"><a href="https://bit.ly/ISO24896%20">ISO 24896:2026 Notation for business reporting</a></span></span> in June 2026. This is the first international standard to set consistent design requirements for the visual notation of business reports: charts, tables, and text elements. It was developed to improve the clarity, consistency, and efficiency of business communication worldwide by establishing a common notation for written reports, presentations, and dashboards. </p><p>While not a part of the ISO-24495 series, the work was done by the same working group and builds on the principles of ISO 24495-1.</p><p>The initiative was led by the <a href="https://www.ibcs.com/">IBCS Association</a>, which maintains the IBCS (International Business Communication Standards) framework.</p><p> </p><h2><span style="font-size: xx-large;">Part 4 and on</span></h2><p><span style="font-size: 19px; background-color: #ffffff;">ISO is developing a part that will enable an organization to certify that it “</span><a href="https://www.iso.org/standard/90061.html?browse=tc" style="font-size: 19px; background: #ffffff;"><span style="font-size: 19px; text-decoration: underline;">uses plain language systematically in its operations</span>.</a><span style="font-size: 19px; background-color: #ffffff;">” </span>ISO is also developing more parts to its plain language standard, including document design.  </p></div></div><div id="Implementing" class="et_pb_with_border et_pb_module et_pb_text et_pb_text_5  et_pb_text_align_left et_pb_bg_layout_light"><div class="et_pb_text_inner"><h2><span style="font-size: xx-large;">Implementing the standard</span></h2><p>To help you follow the standard and apply it to your documents, the Federation has created some resources, such as testimonials, case studies, and other supporting documents.</p><h3><span style="font-size: x-large;"><strong></strong></span></h3><h3><span style="font-size: x-large;"><strong>Repository of supporting documents</strong></span></h3><p>Supporting documents are not published by ISO but they can help you implement the ISO plain language standard, both the general principles in Part 1 and more detailed provisions in other parts. </p><h3><span style="font-size: x-large;"><strong></strong></span></h3></div></div><div class="et_pb_button_module_wrapper et_pb_button_1_wrapper  et_pb_module "> <a class="et_pb_button et_pb_button_1 et_animated et_hover_enabled et_pb_bg_layout_light" href="https://graphicdesign-research.com/IPLF/index.html" data-icon="$" data-animation-style="fade" data-animation-repeat="" data-animation-duration="1000ms" data-animation-delay="0ms" data-animation-intensity="50%" data-animation-starting-opacity="0%" data-animation-speed-curve="ease-in-out">Repository of supporting documents</a></div><div id="Implementing" class="et_pb_with_border et_pb_module et_pb_text et_pb_text_6  et_pb_text_align_left et_pb_bg_layout_light"><div class="et_pb_text_inner"><h3><span style="font-size: x-large;"><strong>Certification</strong></span></h3><p>The current standard is for guidance only and is not for certification. We’ve established a Certification Committee that’s exploring options about this topic.</p><h3><span style="font-size: x-large;"><strong></strong></span></h3><h3><span style="font-size: x-large;"><strong>Testimonials</strong></span></h3><p>We’ve collected <span style="text-decoration: underline;"><a href="https://www.iplfederation.org/testimonials">testimonials</a></span> from people who are using the standard in real-world situations. If you have a testimonial you’d like us to publish, email it to <a href="chair@iplfederation.org"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">chair@iplfederation.org</span></a>.</p><h3><span style="font-size: x-large;"><strong></strong></span></h3><h3><span style="font-size: x-large;"><strong>Case studies</strong></span></h3><p>Many people ask for real-world examples that show how plain language works. We’re publishing some plain language case studies from around the world. These outline how various organizations have successfully used the ISO standard as part of a plain language project.</p><ul><li><a href="https://www.iplfederation.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/ISO-Case-Study_Australian-Taxation-Office.pdf"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Australia: Australia Taxation Office — useful tips for using their new website</span></a></li><li><a href="https://www.iplfederation.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/ISO-Case-Study_Primary-Aldosteronism-Brochures.pdf"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Australia: Primary aldosteronism explained</span></a></li><li><a href="https://www.iplfederation.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/ISO-Case-Study_CCSA.pdf"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Canada: Guidance on alcohol and health</span></a></li><li><a href="https://www.iplfederation.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Case-Study-From-Academia-to-Practice.pdf"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Canada: From Academia to Practice</span></a></li><li><a href="https://www.iplfederation.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Case-study-Part-2-Anush-Sukiasyan_final.pdf"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Spain: Applying ISO 24495-2 to improve legal communications in the luxury sector</span></a><span style="text-decoration: underline;"></span></li></ul><p>If you have a case study you’d like us to publish, follow the case study guide below and then email it to <a href="chair@iplfederation.org"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">chair@iplfederation.org</span></a>.</p><h3><span style="font-size: x-large;"><strong></strong></span></h3><h3><span style="font-size: x-large;"><strong>Case study guide</strong></span></h3><p>Our detailed case study guide gives you a straightforward, step-by-step approach to start your plain language initiative.</p><p><a href="https://www.iplfederation.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Creating-case-studies-_step-by-step-guide_V7-Oct-2024.pdf"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Creating case studies: a step-by-step guide</span></a></p><h3><span style="font-size: x-large;"><strong></strong></span></h3></div></div><div id="Implementing" class="et_pb_with_border et_pb_module et_pb_text et_pb_text_7  et_pb_text_align_left et_pb_bg_layout_light"><div class="et_pb_text_inner"><h3><span style="font-size: x-large;"><strong>Countries can endorse, adopt or sell the standard</strong></span></h3><p><span style="font-size: 19px;">A country’s standards body that is a member of ISO can either endorse the standard (just say they agree with the standard as it is), or they can adopt the standard as a national standard for their country.</span></p><p>Some countries choose to just refer to ISO standards rather than endorse or adopt them. Those countries often sell ISO standards that they have not endorsed or adopted.</p><p>National standards bodies around the world are <span style="text-decoration: underline;"><a href="https://www.iplfederation.org/standard-translations/">translating, localizing and adopting the plain language standard</a></span>. Within 2 years of its publication, 14 translated it and 21 countries had adopted it or were selling it.</p><h3><span style="font-size: x-large;"><strong></strong></span></h3><h3><span style="font-size: x-large;"><strong>Get involved </strong></span></h3><p>If you want to learn more about how your country can adopt the standard, or how to join the team advocating for adopting and using the standard, read these short guidance documents:</p><ul><li><a href="https://www.iplfederation.org/how-iso-works"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">How ISO works: an overview and how you can be involved</span></a></li><li><a href="https://www.iplfederation.org/adopting-guide"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Guide to adopting the ISO plain language standard</span></a></li><li><a href="https://www.iplfederation.org/adopting-checklist"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Checklist for adopting the ISO plain language standard</span></a></li></ul><p>You can also join the localization and implementation committee: message us through the contact form at the bottom of this page.</p></div></div><div id="History" class="et_pb_module et_pb_text et_pb_text_8  et_pb_text_align_left et_pb_bg_layout_light"><div class="et_pb_text_inner"><h2><span><span style="font-size: xx-large;"><strong></strong></span></span></h2><h2><span style="font-size: xx-large;">History</span></h2><p>Plain language practitioners began formally discussing options for creating an international standard in 2007. Read about <a href="https://www.iplfederation.org/history-plain-language/"><span style="text-decoration: underline;">how the ISO plain language standard was developed</span></a>.</p><p><span><span
